newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania c.bank forex reserves at $1.6 billion - PM.
newsitem.headline: Romania c.bank forex reserves at $1.6 billion - PM.

text.p: Romanian Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea said on Tuesday the country's central bank reserves had risen to $1.6 billion, more than double the level in February, following tough reforms launched by his government this year.
"In February, the central bank had 700 billion lei and $700 million. Today its reserves amount to 1.6 trillion lei and $1.6 billion," Ciorbea told a news conference.
He made the remarks in a state-of-the-nation report marking almost six months since his centrist government took office.
May's is the highest foreign exchange reserve level recorded in post-communist Romania. Last month, the central bank (BNR) said its reserves stood at $1.45 billion.

Ciorbea said the economic reforms launched in February had helped the BNR to, "accumulate a significant reserve meant to keep the monetary policy under control and allow the relaunch of the economy." Of the $1.6 billion some $265 million came from the population, $315 million from direct foreign investments and $300 million from repatriation of export earnings.
"One should also add an estimated $150-$200 million in portfolio investments," he said.
"These figures confirm that Romania has entered the system of interests of the big markets and that there is full trust in the government and its programme," Ciorbea added.
Increasing foreign exchange reserves is among the main targets of the government's shock-therapy programme, also endorsed by international lenders.
Over the past months, BNR has bought large amounts of dollars to build up reserves, as well as to prevent the leu from firming.
Analysts warned a firmer leu could have a negative impact on reforms, affecting mainly exports and restructuring.
The leu has been trading in a relatively stable range near 7,050 to the dollar this month after recovering from a record low of 9,000 in mid-February.
Last month, the International Monetary Fund released the a first $86 million tranche of a $430 million stand-by accord.

The BNR hopes further IMF tranches, purchases from the local market and a bond issue by Romania's Finance Ministry for around 700 million marks next month could push its reserves beyond $2 billion in June.
